lines: Somebody from the Concord copied out nine years of my marks last week.
Very polite. Asked if I'd consider stopping. Said the record wasn't informative.
I marked it again this morning. Same line. Ninety-four days.
I mark the high tide on that post every morning. Nine years running.
The mark hasn't moved since the first week of spring.
Not higher. Not lower. The same line, ninety-odd days.
The sea does not do that on its own.
Eleven pans, filled on the spring tide and left to the sun. Six weeks and you have salt.
Salthollow cures its hides with it, Tideglass salts its fish with it, and the barrels go up the ridge.
Or they did. There has been no cart for mine in three weeks. The road is full of somebody else.
Eleven pans, filled on the spring tide and left to the sun. Six weeks and you have salt.
One puddle of seawater, three trades and a village. Nobody ever believes me.
Mind the walls. They are a hand wide and they are four hundred years old.
Empty going down, loaded coming back. Wrong way round, that, and it has been all season.
Everything on this coast used to come out of Tideglass and go inland.
Now it comes down off the ridge and goes into Tideglass, and none of it comes out again.
